So evamāha: He says: ‘ettakā usabhā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā vacchatarā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā vacchatariyo haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā ajā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā urabbhā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā assā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā rukkhā chijjantu yūpatthāya, ettakā dabbhā lūyantu barihisatthāyā’ti. ‘Slaughter this many bulls, bullocks, heifers, goats, rams, and horses for the sacrifice!
And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

folded.id: take up|the|training and livelihood of the mendicants
folded.subject: take up
folded.object: training and livelihood of the mendicants

spans.text: Once they’ve gone forth, they take up the training and livelihood of the mendicants.

It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.
He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased.

folded.id: then pessa|the|elephant marshal’s son and kandaraka the wanderer went to the buddha
folded.subject: Then Pessa
folded.object: elephant marshal’s son and Kandaraka the wanderer went to the Buddha

spans.text: Then Pessa the elephant marshal’s son and Kandaraka the wanderer went to the Buddha.
They’re scrupulous and kind, living full of sympathy for all living beings.

folded.id: to lead|the|spiritual life utterly full and pure
folded.subject: to lead
folded.object: spiritual life utterly full and pure

spans.text: It’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.
His bondservants, servants, and workers do their jobs under threat of punishment and danger, weeping with tearful faces.

folded.id: why|don’t|i shave off my hair and beard
folded.subject: Why
folded.object: I shave off my hair and beard

spans.text: Yannūnāhaṁ kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajeyyan’ti. Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’
He shaves off his hair and beard, dresses in a rough antelope hide, and smears his body with ghee and oil.

jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; They refrain from receiving gold and currency, āmakadhaññapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; raw grains, āmakamaṁsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; raw meat, itthikumārikapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; women and girls, dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; male and female bondservants, ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; goats and sheep, kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; chickens and pigs, Adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena su
